---
title: Hive native Cloudflare migration
description: Move Hive UI, APIs, worlds and background work off on-premise, Supabase and Vercel in verified stages.
---

## Outcome and current boundaries

The target is a working Hive research application fully hosted on Cloudflare,
with no on-premise service, Hive Postgres, Supabase or Vercel dependency in its
accepted production request/job graph. A UI upload alone does not meet that
outcome. Maintenance is an independent interim response; see the
[approval-gated maintenance runbook](/build/devops/hive-cloudflare-maintenance).

Current source, rather than old deployment prose, defines the starting graph:

| Capability | Current owner | Cloudflare target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hidden-locale Next.js host, login handoff, editor | `apps/hive`, `packages/hive-ui` | Vite+ UI and Worker host with equivalent bilingual routes |
| Product API | `apps/hive/src/app/api/v1/hive` | Hive Worker adapters over portable domain services |
| Shared client contract | `packages/internal-api/src/hive.ts` | Preserve typed public exports and response/error shapes |
| World snapshots, events, economy, research, NPCs | `apps/hive/src/lib/hive/hive-db.ts`, `HIVE_DATABASE_URL` | One authoritative transactional store per invariant; D1 and SQLite-backed DOs after contract qualification |
| Yjs sync and presence | `apps/hive-realtime`, `packages/realtime` | One hibernating WebSocket DO per server |
| Membership, platform roles and workspace context | Hive access adapter plus main platform APIs/Supabase | Consent-aware Cloudflare identity/access service under its owning platform lane |
| AI credits and model calls | Hive AI adapters and platform credit service | Portable model/credit adapter with Cloudflare durable budget reservation |
| Simulation and workflow execution | Hive routes and optional local model origin | Bounded Worker/Queue/Workflow execution; no local inference dependency |
| Static assets and research exports | App public assets and export handlers | Worker static assets; private R2 only where size/retention requires it |

The live tunnel was read-only inspected with a healthy connector but Hive routed
to port 7814; realtime's source default is 7815. Source execution/deployed identity,
the exact stopped process and its data freshness remain unverified because the
origin machine is outside this lane's custody. Export/import needs a separately
authorized data owner; never inspect its host or credentials as a shortcut.

Read-only hostname-filtered Cloudflare adaptive analytics observed Hive 502s
at least as far back as 26 September 2026 at 18:00 (GMT+7). The returned
30-day groups contain no origin 2xx; occasional edge 200s with origin status 0
do not prove origin recovery. Sampling and the start of the available window
leave the exact onset unknown. The outage predates the later tunnel-token
rotation. This observation does not establish which source or process was live.

## Contracts to preserve before changing hosts

Hive servers are global research worlds. Workspace selection supplies AI context
and billing, not a world-data filter. Enabled members can join enabled servers;
platform admins retain explicit privileged actions. Preserve the shared editor
between the satellite and embedded web host, access requests, session expiry,
refresh/logout, actor attribution and server-bound realtime tokens.

Extract domain and persistence interfaces from Next/Bun adapters before replacing
them. Portable entrypoints must not import Next.js, React Router, Cloudflare
request globals, SQL clients or framework session stores. Inject actor, storage,
clock, model client, navigation and localization at adapters. Migrate actual
callers together and delete legacy interfaces rather than adding an unused
compatibility facade. Existing public package exports stay stable.

The source uses Postgres transactions, JSONB, UUIDs, binary CRDT state and runtime
schema initialization. Port these explicitly: versioned D1/DO migrations, bound
queries, normalized indexed fields, supported JSON representation and binary
encoding. Never carry runtime DDL into a request or pretend SQLite is Postgres.
Source tables are not evidence that every store holds identical live data.

## Authoritative state and consistency

Start by qualifying one representative world/event transaction and one trade
transaction against real D1/DO storage on staging. Preserve atomic snapshot/event
sequence, actor checks, duplicate operation handling, research associations,
currency conservation and inventory ownership. Yjs convergence must not settle
currency, AI charges or ownership.

Select one authority for each invariant. Proposed default: a server DO orders
realtime operations and holds the Yjs document/op sequence; D1 holds durable
relational product data. An atomic requirement spanning DO and D1 must use a
persisted outbox and idempotent consumer with a defined acknowledgement point,
or be colocated in one store. Never acknowledge an event as durable in one
store while its required audit/ledger row can be lost in the other. Cross-server
economy transactions remain in a single D1 transactional boundary where they
must conserve value; prove the actual API supports the required transaction
before selecting it. Otherwise revise the schema/ownership before migration.

Use operation IDs generated once by the caller and retained across uncertain
retries. Persist deduplication and progress with the authoritative write.
Unknown outcomes reconcile by the same ID; they are never replayed with a new
ID. Revision conflicts, concurrent writers and partial failure stay explicit.

## Authentication and data migration

The first staging host may use the existing centralized login handoff as a
temporary bridge, with its Supabase dependency clearly recorded. That does not
qualify a fully Cloudflare cutover. Final acceptance requires the platform owner
to provide Cloudflare-native identity, membership, role/workspace and credit
contracts with equivalent revocation, workspace consent and deletion fences.
Preserve app-local cookies, audience checks, CSRF protection, bounded token
lifetime and no raw service-secret fallback for realtime signing.

Before any data write, the data owner inventories authoritative source tables,
counts, relationships, schema versions, latest operation sequences and private
export checksums. Decide authority from live callers plus owner evidence, not
table names. Export privately with no secrets/customer data in repository or CI
artifacts. Keep source originals and a tested restore until acceptance.

Import in bounded batches using a durable manifest, source checksum, cursor and
idempotent row key. Verify counts/checksums, relationships, binary CRDT round trips,
ledger sums, member decisions and sampled authorized queries. A failed batch
records partial progress and can resume without duplicates. Drain/fence legacy
writers under their owner's custody for the final delta and verify the fence.
If that owner cannot perform the export/fence without this lane accessing the
restricted host, migration is blocked; keep maintenance live.

## Billable work and durable stop fence

Staging defaults to all autonomous simulation/model work disabled. Before enabling
any scheduler, reserve a finite per-run and per-server budget durably: maximum
ticks, NPCs, turns, requests, tokens, money, attempts and deadline. Enforce payload,
fan-out, concurrency and WebSocket message/room limits at ingress and storage.
Retries consume the original budget; crash/restart never resets it.

A durable generation/stop record is checked before enqueue, dequeue, each model
or storage side effect, and before scheduling the next alarm. Stopped, exhausted,
deleted, consent-revoked and terminal runs schedule nothing further. Stale queued
messages are acknowledged without work; deletion tombstones outlive delayed
messages. Bounded progress checkpoints retain operation identity. A stop cannot
recall a model call already issued: reserve its entire possible charge before
the call, cap time/tokens and report any unsettled reservation honestly.

Test operation counts on success, retries, repeated delivery, crash between
reservation/write/ack, restart, queue delay and stop during in-flight work.
Prove stale alarms/messages cannot restart a stopped generation and budgets
cannot go negative or reset. Record counts and stop latency through the owning
adoption runbook. Rate limiting, CPU caps and billing alerts supplement this
fence; none is a total-spend guarantee. No paid service provisioning occurs
without its separately granted spending authority.

## Small PR and delivery sequence

| Unit | Scope | Exit evidence and rollback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Maintenance Worker and this plan | Reviewed source, focused tests, approved runtime/routing packet; delete only the new route/script or restore captured bodies |
| 1 | Domain/persistence/auth adapter seams and source truth | Existing caller behavior/negative controls pass; revert scoped extraction without data writes |
| 2 | D1/DO schema and a representative transaction | Real staging persistence, concurrency, idempotency and migration restart tests; disposable staging stores only |
| 3 | Hibernating realtime DO | Two clients converge; reconnect/restart preserves op sequence; revoked/wrong-server tokens rejected; no empty-room alarm loop |
| 4 | Vite+ UI/Worker host and full API parity | Exact-source build artifact, real Worker runtime and bilingual browser flows; staging route only |
| 5 | Durable budgets, stop fence, scheduler/model adapters | Failure/restart/stop operation-count tests; real platform auth/credit contracts; no Supabase/Vercel/on-prem edges in accepted graph |
| 6 | Authorized import, final delta, scoped canonical cutover | Owner-exported manifest, reconciliation, browser acceptance, exact deployment identity and rollback rehearsal |

Keep independent changes in separate PRs; dependent layers use native GitHub
stacks when supported. No PR in this lane merges itself. Review deployment,
identity, permissions, data and spend boundaries independently before integration.
Gates run on the authorized Thanh runner in `_work.noindex`, through `ttr`,
with observed load at most 30. No local release builds or restricted-host access.

## Staging, cutover and rollback acceptance

1. Admit staging resources/hostname and spending scope separately. Publish an
   immutable exact-commit artifact; run the actual Worker and DO runtime, then
   browser checks with disposable identities. Keep provenance and config/binding
   IDs private. Require applicable exact-head CI checks and build evidence.
2. Exercise login/refresh/logout, approved/restricted/admin identities, both
   locales, two-client world edits, reconnect, research export, economy and
   billing failures. Verify no cookies or API traffic reaches a retired host.
3. Rehearse stop and rollback with the same release candidate. Set thresholds
   from measured staging baselines before promotion: failed auth, invariant
   mismatch, ledger discrepancy, unexpected egress or uncontrolled operation
   count blocks cutover. Readiness requires product-owner acceptance, not only
   healthy HTTP responses.
4. Take a Hive-only promotion window with the integration/data owners; preserve
   Finance's lane. Fence writers, apply final delta and verify reconciliation.
   Route only Hive to the accepted Worker; retain the maintenance script and
   captured DNS/tunnel states. No shared-zone wildcard or main-host change.
5. If acceptance fails, switch Hive back to maintenance and stop new jobs using
   the durable fence. Preserve Cloudflare writes for reconciliation. Restore a
   previous working app only when data compatibility and writer authority are
   proven; DNS reversal alone is insufficient once new writes are accepted.
   Never roll back to an unverified down origin as a claim of restored service.
6. Observe a finite owner-agreed window and record exact source/deployment,
   migration manifests, stop tests and customer-facing results. Retire old
   resources only after accepted data retention/deletion decisions. Completion
   requires the whole accepted runtime graph to be Cloudflare-native.
